content: The document provides a detailed analysis of the efficacy and safety of oral antiviral agents for COVID-19, based on data collected up to August 8, 2022. The findings are presented in a series of forest plots, each corresponding to specific outcomes. Below are the descriptions of the outcomes analyzed: 1. All-cause mortality (28-day follow-up): A forest plot (Figure 1) compares the use of oral antiviral agents to no antiviral treatment, focusing on the impact on all-cause mortality within 28 days of follow-up. 2. COVID-19-related hospitalizations (28-day follow-up): Figure 2 illustrates the comparison between oral antiviral treatment and no treatment, specifically evaluating the reduction in hospitalizations related to COVID-19 within the same 28-day period. 3. COVID-19-related hospitalizations or all-cause death (28-day follow-up): Figure 3 combines the outcomes of hospitalizations and all-cause mortality, comparing the effectiveness of oral antivirals versus no treatment over 28 days. 4. Serious adverse events: Figure 4 examines the incidence of serious adverse events in patients receiving oral antivirals compared to those who did not receive such treatment. 5. Serious adverse events related to the drug or placebo: Figure 5 focuses on serious adverse events specifically attributed to the oral antiviral agents or the placebo, providing a more targeted safety analysis. 6. All respiratory interventions (through day 29): Figure 6 evaluates the need for any respiratory intervention (e.g., oxygen therapy, mechanical ventilation) in patients treated with oral antivirals versus those without treatment, up to day 29. 7. Invasive mechanical ventilation (MV), noninvasive MV, or high-flow oxygen device: Figure 7 compares the requirement for advanced respiratory support (invasive or noninvasive mechanical ventilation, or high-flow oxygen devices) between the two groups. 8. Invasive mechanical ventilation (MV): Figure 8 specifically assesses the need for invasive mechanical ventilation in patients treated with oral antivirals compared to those who did not receive such treatment. Each of these outcomes is analyzed using Review Manager (RevMan) software version 5.4.1, which is a standard tool for conducting meta-analyses in clinical research. The results provide a comprehensive evaluation of the benefits and risks associated with oral antiviral agents for COVID-19.
